PRIVACY & DATA HANDLING

A small footprint.
Clear boundaries.

Skim’s extension processes reading content on your device. It does not send that content to the developer.

Effective November 6, 2026 · Skim Reading Lens beta 0.2.1

The Chrome extension

The extension highlights original sentences on webpages you activate and can open selected text or a rendered article in its local reader. On a ChatGPT page, explicit reader import first tries the latest rendered assistant response. Page content may include personal or sensitive material from the page you choose, so it is processed only for the reading features.

DataUse and locationRetention
Paragraph text and pointer interactionsUsed in the current page to choose a sentence locally. No developer upload or interaction log.Working memory while the lens runs.
Explicitly imported text and titlePassed to the extension reader using Chrome session storage, then consumed and removed. The text itself is not put in the URL.Temporary handoff; removed on consumption. Abandoned handoffs are cleared on the next import or browser session reset.
Reader text and pinned sentencesHeld in the reader tab. No account, cloud copy, or history.Until the reader tab is reloaded or closed.
Reading goal, pause and dock preferencesSaved in Chrome’s local extension storage.Until reset, changed, or the extension is removed.
Remembered site patternsScheme and hostname patterns saved locally to enable the lens on those sites. They are not a log of pages you visit.Until you forget the site, revoke access, or remove the extension.

The extension does not transmit page text, browsing activity, pointer coordinates, or preferences to the developer. It has no analytics, ads, sale of data, account system, camera access, or model-provider calls. It does not execute remotely hosted code.

Limited use

Skim uses webpage content and interaction information only to provide its visible reading features. It does not sell or transfer that data, use it for advertising, or provide it to people for review. The extension’s use of data is limited to its stated reading purpose, consistent with the Chrome Web Store User Data Policy and its Limited Use requirements.

Permissions and your control

activeTab allows deliberate use on the current tab. scripting inserts the local reader tools. storage keeps preferences and the temporary text handoff. Optional host access is requested only when you choose to remember a site. Chrome’s host permission patterns apply to the chosen scheme and hostname, across paths and ports.

Use the dock to pause or close the current lens. Use extension settings to pause all sites or forget a remembered site and revoke its permission. You can also control site access or remove Skim at chrome://extensions. Removing the extension clears its local storage. The hosted lab uses browser permissions independently, so revoke any camera permission separately in browser site settings.

This website and the reading lab

The website does not add analytics, advertising cookies, or an account system. Text you paste in the reading lab stays in the page’s memory and is not uploaded by Skim. Normal website hosting may process request metadata such as IP address, browser details, requested files, and access times under the hosting provider’s policies. Skim does not control the provider’s log retention.

If you explicitly start experimental webcam gaze, the lab first asks for consent, then loads a pinned copy of WebGazer and its face-model assets from this website. The website host receives ordinary asset requests; the tracker does not fetch code or models from a third-party CDN at runtime. The camera frames and estimated gaze coordinates are processed in your browser; Skim does not record or upload them. The lab disables WebGazer’s persistent calibration storage. Stop, switch modes, hide the tab, or close the page to end the camera session. You can revoke site camera permission in Chrome.

The compatibility check can load and initialize the same tracking files after you click its button, while keeping the camera off. Its result stays on that page and is not sent as a report.

The webcam lab is separate from the extension. Opening it does not transfer the current webpage’s text. It estimates screen regions, cannot reliably know the exact word you read, and does not measure comprehension. The library is experimental and device accuracy remains unvalidated.

Optional developer Jev integration

The source package includes an optional localhost server. If a developer supplies their own TypeSafe API key and explicitly enables Jev in that local reader, it sends the selected paragraph’s candidate sentences, reading goal, and focus words to TypeSafe for a sentence choice. Provider terms, retention policies, and charges apply. It does not send camera frames or gaze coordinates. Jev is not used by the downloadable consumer extension or this hosted demo.

Feedback and changes

The help page can generate a blank feedback template locally. It does not submit a report or automatically collect page content, device identifiers, or browsing history. Share reports voluntarily and remove sensitive material first.

For support, privacy questions, or private security reports, use the address below. Public bug reports belong in GitHub Issues. Do not include private page content in a public issue.

Changes to this policy will be published here with a new effective date. Material changes to permissions or data use will be reflected in the extension and its store disclosures. Review the source code or visit Help for current limitations.
